description: Stakeholder-Specific Vulnerability Categorization decision framework for vulnerability triage. Apply this decision tree to each vulnerability affecting the software inventory.

exploitation.description: Evidence of active exploitation in the wild

values.active: Exploitation attempts have been observed in network traffic analysis

automatable.description: Whether an attacker can reliably automate exploitation across many targets without target-specific reconnaissance
automatable.determination: A vulnerability is automatable if ALL of the following CVSS v3.1 base metric conditions are met: Attack Vector is NETWORK (AV:N), Attack Complexity is LOW (AC:L), and User Interaction is NONE (UI:N). If any condition is not met, the vulnerability is not automatable.

values.yes: All conditions met - attack is automatable
values.no: One or more conditions not met - requires manual effort or specific conditions

technical_impact.description: Severity of the technical impact if the vulnerability is exploited
technical_impact.determination: Impact is 'total' if ALL THREE of Confidentiality, Integrity, and Availability impact metrics in the CVSS v3.1 base vector are HIGH. Otherwise impact is 'partial'.

values.total: Complete compromise of confidentiality, integrity, and availability
values.partial: Limited impact - not all CIA dimensions are fully compromised

mission_prevalence.description: How critical the affected asset is to the organization's mission
mission_prevalence.determination: Determined by the mission_prevalence field in mission_impact.json for the affected inventory item(s). When a CVE affects multiple inventory items, use the highest mission prevalence among them.

values.high: Asset is essential to core mission functions
values.medium: Asset supports important but non-critical functions

decision_tree.description: Traverse top-to-bottom; first matching rule determines the decision.
